newsitem.title: UK: EMU risk to exchanges seen rising - rating agencies.
newsitem.headline: EMU risk to exchanges seen rising - rating agencies.

text.p: Concerns over the threat posed to financial exchanges and clearing houses by European economic and monetary union are rising, according to credit rating agencies at an industry conference on Thursday.
If the euro starts on time in 1999, it will effectively remove separate debt instruments for those countries which take part in a single currency -- slashing the number of financial products.

"If EMU takes place, it could mean the elimination of 60 percent of Europe related business, and increase competition among the exchanges," said Leslie Muranyi, senior analyst, financial institutions, at Moody's Investor's Services.

He said the competition among institutions to attract members in a shrinking pool could lead to a more relaxed attitude to controls and regulations, as potential exchange members shop around for the best deal.
"As competition grows, clearing houses must strike a balance between prudent standards and attracting members," he said. "The trade off is the clearing houses' dilemma."
Rating clearing houses and exchanges is more complex than rating other businesses, the agencies said, since they are not run to make a profit and typically have only one line of business.

Standard & Poor's rates four such institutions, the Board of Trade Clearing Corp, Cedel bank, Mercado de Valores de Buenos Aires, and the Options Clearing Corporation. Of these, all have investment grade ratings except Mercado de Valores.
S&P's Jake Newman, director financial institutions, said an important issue in assessing credit worthiness is therefore to look at factors such as implicit government and member support.
He said, as EMU approaches, there appears to be a general assumption that any local exchange which winds up business, will do so without any problems.
"But there is the possibility of a blow up at the worst possible time -- when the clearing members are heading for the exits," he said.
